title: Duplicate entry for `Ctrl` Key when mapping an event to action using Event Configuration window
body:
### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.0.stable and later ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700K CPU @ 4.00GHz (8 threads) - 14.94 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Adding Ctrl key using Event Configuration window by searching for it shows two identical entries under Keyboard Events, clicking on either one shows no difference in their properties (for example, one being for Left Ctrl, other being Right Ctrl), instead showing as "neutral" Ctrl (which corresponds to both Left AND Right Ctrl key). I have no clue if it's an intended feature, as testing from my end shows this exact behaviour dating back to 4.0 release of Godot (checkout screenshots below). > [!NOTE] > This only happens to `Ctrl` for some reason, I couldn't reproduce this with, lets say, `shift` key. > > Adding one of the resulted `Ctrl` event, and then adding the other afterward doesn't link two separate events to same action, instead it'll links only one Ctrl. which seems confirmed by Godot itself when trying to add the second `Ctrl` key, displaying an Error `Error: This action already contains this input event`.
Screenshots

From 4.7

From 4.6.3

From 4.0

### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any Godot 4.x executable. 2. Create an project through the project manager. 3. Click on `Project -> Project Settings` and navigate to `Input Map` tab and Left click it. 4. Add a new action with any name you like (lets call it `MyCtrl`) in the `Add New Action` Input field, and press `+ Add` button. 5. `MyCtrl` will be shown, on the Right of it you'll see a `+` button, click it to add an Event which corresponds (or "links") a specific set of Input Events to an Input Action. 6. You'll see a window pops up, titled `Event Configuration for "MyCtrl"`, inside you'll see two fields, one listens to any input you make, and another for filtering available input events. Issue with the filtering/searching for specific events. Type in the second field (the `Filter Inputs` one) the following: `Ctrl` 7. See 2 identical results, which may be confusing for new users of the engine, as there's no obvious difference between them ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [testing-ctrl-key.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30200770/testing-ctrl-key.zip) > [!NOTE] > on line `26` of `project.godot` file, you'll notice `"physical_keycode"` is equal to `4194326`, which's indeed `KEY_CTRL` enum constant found in the docs ([link](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_@globalscope.html#enum-globalscope-key)).
